content: A preauricular cyst is a congenital anomaly that connects to the external surface via a sinus tract, which opens into a small pit located just anterior to the root of the helix of the ear. In some cases, this pit may discharge foul-smelling material. When a preauricular cyst becomes infected, it may require incision and drainage. However, definitive surgical excision of the cyst is typically delayed until the cyst has refilled to allow for proper identification and removal. In pediatric cases of infected preauricular cysts, initial treatment often involves the administration of antibiotics to manage the infection. Surgical excision is then performed at a later stage. During the surgical excision, both the sinus tract and the cyst are carefully removed. To facilitate this process, methylene blue dye is injected into the pit to outline the tract and cyst, ensuring complete excision.
